GNET - 4E & diff judgements - basic analysis

GNET - 4 elements with difference ratings from participants

This is the analysis of the second run of GNET4E. Everything is the same, except that in the study phase participants looked at a familiar first then a novel and rated the subjective difference of the images.

As in the original task, stimuli were algorithmically generated, allowing precise comparison between stimuli. The difference between the stimulus presented and other stimuli (several comparisons are used) is a proxy for novelty.

During familiarization, participants learned a set of 5 stimuli During the study phase, they rated the difference of these stimuli to novels. During the test phase, the performed a recognition memory test for the novels intermixed with distractors. - Novels and distractors were balanced.

In the original GNET, recognition performance tended to increase monotonically with difference to familiars In the GNET4E participants showed their highest categorization performance for stimuli at intermediate levels of difference.

Difference indices

Exclusions

We excluded 5 participants due to a high number of missed responses in the study phase (≥ 20).

We excluded 5 participants due to a high number of missed responses in the recognition test (> 33).

We excluded 0 participants due to inattention to task details, indicated by a mean difference judgment > 5 for prototype– prototype comparisons.

This left 49 participants in the analysis.

The identifiers are:

501_179, 502_178, 503_180, 504_190, 505_189, 506_181, 507_187, 508_192, 510_191, 511_193, 514_198, 515_199, 516_200, 517_202, 518_204, 519_203, 520_205, 522_207, 523_208, 524_210, 526_212, 527_213, 528_214, 529_215, 530_240, 531_253, 532_259, 533_262, 534_308, 535_323, 536_324, 537_391, 539_342, 540_343, 543_367, 544_371, 547_385, 551_407, 554_423, 557_435, 558_446, 559_449, 560_451, 561_453, 562_456, 564_458, 565_459, 566_462, 567_465

Study phase

Participants make a judgement of the difference between a prototype and a novel picture.

Test phase

Test phase was the same as before: participants see the novel pictures from the study phase with distractors from the same categories. They signal if they think the picture is an old one from the study phase, or a novel distractor.

ALT - Mixed models

Use sum-to-zero contrasts so that coefficients are interpreted as deviations from the grand mean rather than comparisons with the reference level (D1). This is useful when no stimulus type serves as a theoretically meaningful baseline condition.
